text:
tasha: Heads up 1: we found an unexpected KMS grant on alias/rd-backups that grants Decrypt to an external account (arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/external-backup). Not created by the infra team. Marking for immediate triage.
ben: Yikes. How was it discovered?
tasha: Alert from the KMS audit rule: list-grants returned a grant with a strange name and grant-creation metadata shows created-by=backup-plugin-v0.9.2. That plugin runs in our CI pipeline for ad-hoc tenant exports.
iris: Paste the minimal list-grants output I saw: ```text
$ aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/rd-backups
GRANT  id: ab12-34cd  granteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/external-backup  operations: [Decrypt]  creationDate: 2026-05-17T07:18:12Z  retiringPrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-admin
```
sec-eng: That looks like an orphaned grant created by a pipeline job using the plugin. First steps: (A) retire/revoke the grant immediately, (B) snapshot grant list for audit, (C) identify which pipeline run created it, (D) rotate CMK if we see any suspicious GET/Object access tied to that grant.
ben: Exec commands to revoke: ```bash
aws kms revoke-grant --key-id alias/rd-backups --grant-id ab12-34cd
# if revoke fails, retire as last resort
aws kms retire-grant --key-id alias/rd-backups --grant-id ab12-34cd --grant-token <token-from-create>
```
forensics-bot: Suggested CloudTrail lookup (pseudo): ```sql
SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.arn, eventName, requestParameters, sourceIPAddress
FROM cloudtrail_events
WHERE eventName IN ('CreateGrant','RetireGrant','RevokeGrant') AND requestParameters.keyId LIKE '%rd-backups%'
AND eventTime >= '2026-05-10T00:00:00Z'
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
LIMIT 200
```
tasha: I already revoked the grant (just did). Moving next to scope: checking whether that external principal used the grant to decrypt anything. Forensics: search Decrypt events where userIdentity.arn == that grantee or where requestParameters.keyId == alias/rd-backups.
iris: Quick query returned three Decrypt events between 2026-05-17T07:20Z and 2026-05-17T08:15Z by sourceIPAddress 54.33.22.11 (unrecognized). We're pulling S3 GETs for snapshot objects around that time.
enforcement: If decrypts used that grant, we escalate to legal and customer-notify triage.
legal: Please preserve chain-of-custody. Do not delete logs. We'll need the forensics export and timeline before we decide on disclosure.
ben: Root cause hypothesis: backup-plugin-v0.9.2 has a feature that auto-creates temporary grants for third-party export, and the pipeline runs non-interactively with broad privileges. We need to patch plugin, remove auto-grant behavior, and harden who can call CreateGrant in IAM.
sec-eng: Remediations (short-term): 1) revoke/retire any unknown grants (done), 2) revoke any session tokens used by the pipeline run, 3) block the external account via a deny policy on the CMK resource policy, 4) add CloudWatch alerts for CreateGrant on backup CMKs, 5) rotate the CMK if decrypt events confirm data access.
sec-eng: Longer-term: require Change ticket to create any grants; implement IAM condition preventing kms:CreateGrant except from a dedicated admin role, and add a KMS key policy that requires a request tag `ticket_id` for CreateGrant calls (enforced via Condition). Also add pre-deploy static analysis to detect plugin that calls kms:CreateGrant.
iris: Proposed deny snippet (attach to CMK key policy): ```json
{ "Sid": "DenyExternalCreateGrant", "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": "*", "Action": "kms:CreateGrant", "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringNotEquals": { "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-admin" } } }
```
ben: We should be careful: key policy Deniers can lock us out. Suggest an allowlist approach and an admin escape hatch. Also require `kms:ViaService` or `aws:RequestTag/ticket_id` to make grants auditable.
forensics-bot: Export steps: snapshot CloudTrail, S3 access logs, and KMS audit log to a locked archive in the security account. Collect pipeline job history (CI job id) and container image digest used by plugin. Create forensic bucket with restricted access and immutable retention.
legal: Also collect any customer-owned snapshot IDs that appear in the decrypt GETs. We'll need to determine whether customer data may have been exfiltrated. Put customer-notify hold on I-20260517-01.
tasha: Owners: ben -> patch plugin to remove auto-grant and release hotfix; iris -> full audit of CreateGrant calls + correlate CI job; sec-eng -> implement alerting + emergency key policy change to prevent further CreateGrant by non-admins; legal -> hold and review. Forensics-bot -> export logs to sec-archive.
ben: ETA for hotfix: 4h to cut v0.9.3 and push to CI; will add runtime guard to refuse CreateGrant calls unless env var APPROVE_GRANTS=true set by manual step.
iris: ETA for audit export: 2h to produce timeline and CI job artifacts. If decrypts > 0 on external IPs we'll schedule immediate incident call.
sec-eng: After hotfix, we'll run a smoke test: attempt to create grant from pipeline runner (should be denied) and verify CreateGrant metric doesn't spike. Add metric filter for KMS CreateGrant and page sec-oncall if >0 in 15m.
legal: Keep channel updated. Do not destroy any evidence. We'll coordinate customer comms only after we know scope.
forensics-bot: Running export now. Will post S3 GET results and Decrypt event IDs when ready.
tasha: Thanks everyone. Posting CHG-20260517-99 and attaching this thread. We'll reconvene if we get evidence of unauthorized downloads.
